name: GCW Saturday Night SuperFights #1

date.source: The show's own on-screen banner and the post's own dateline.

matches.note: MacGregor (with Brighid McAllister) pins Calamity Sam with the Stirling Spike, a reverse facelock neckbreaker; his first GCW win.
Chaos (with Jennifer Reeves) powerbombs Maniaca through a ringside table, then finishes with the Chaotic Rage spinning powerbomb for the pin.

No winner declared: Ted Bruce stalls backstage and never properly enters, leaving Ruiz to work alone against Canuck until Stanley turns on his own corner, then reconciles with Canuck and Ruiz against Bruce; the broadcast runs out before a fall, no bell, no announced result.

notes: The 2004 revival's own first weekly broadcast ("back after a far-too-long break"). Brandon Simpson attacks a debuting Heath Starr backstage before their scheduled opener can happen, scrubbing the match. Commissioner James Oslo announces a four-way match at the 1 August 2004 pay-per-view WE ALL FALL DOWN (HP Pavilion, San Jose, California, per Oslo's own announcement) to crown a new GCW World Heavyweight Championship, with Starr vs. Simpson at next week's show as the first of four qualifying bouts. A closing tease (a mystery arrival by limo, described only as a former roster member) is not resolved in this wing's own surviving record.

name: GCW Saturday Night SuperFights #2

date.source: The show's own on-screen banner and the post's own dateline.

matches.note: Lacharite pins Rock with a rollup in his own GCW debut.

Ruled a time-limit draw after Stanley outlasts Thorn's own Facebreaker submission hold; Cap'n Canuck (Stanley's corner) spends the match warily circling a seated Aroku Murakami at ringside without incident.

A handicap match: Mark Chaos (with Jennifer Reeves) starts as Ruiz's corner before turning on him mid-match after Juventud Maniaca runs in and kisses Reeves; Ted Bruce pins Ruiz with a foreign-object shot from a miniature refrigerator.

The first of four qualifying bouts for the vacant GCW World Heavyweight Championship. Jordan Thorn runs in for Gorgeous, turns on Simpson with a steel chair he was handed to use on Starr, and Starr pins Simpson after Aroku Murakami separately attacks Simpson at ringside; Starr claims the first of the four championship-match spots.

notes: Broadcast from New York City. Heath Starr defeats Brandon Simpson in a match turned by a Jordan Thorn run-in and a separate Aroku Murakami attack on Simpson, claiming the first of four spots in the vacant GCW World Heavyweight Championship match announced for the 1 August 2004 pay-per-view WE ALL FALL DOWN.

name: GCW Saturday Night SuperFights #3

date.source: The show's own on-screen banner and the post's own dateline; the banner itself is a copy-paste of the previous show's New York/Madison Square Garden banner, an evident production error -- the crowd is explicitly addressed as a sold-out Bell Centre audience in Montreal, Quebec throughout the broadcast, which this record follows instead.

matches.note: A rematch of the wing's own 19 June card; MacGregor (with Brighid McAllister) wins.
Chaos (with Jennifer Reeves) squashes the debuting Capri, driving him through a table and a set of ringsteps before finishing with the Chaotic Rage.

Canuck wins by disqualification after Calamity Sam runs in and attacks him with a broken bottle and a chair; Ken Stanley, drunk, wanders to ringside during the match without further incident. Referee Kazuhito Tokeshi.

Main event and the second of four qualifying bouts for the vacant GCW World Heavyweight Championship. Brandon Simpson (with Gorgeous) interferes -- knocking Thorn out with a bat shot and hitting him with the Punishment, then powerbombing him through a table set over the ringsteps -- clearing the way for Murakami to pin Thorn. Simpson had told a backstage interviewer beforehand that he had arranged for Thorn's opponent to still be able to compete after 'roughing him up' earlier that night; the two accounts do not fully reconcile and are reported as the broadcast presents them. Referee Ron Nord.

notes: Broadcast from Montreal, Quebec (the show's own printed banner is left over from the previous week's New York City card, an evident error; the venue is corrected here from the crowd's own on-air address, not the banner). Aroku Murakami defeats Jordan Thorn in the main event, with a Brandon Simpson interference, to claim the second of four spots in the vacant GCW World Heavyweight Championship match; Simpson separately hands Thorn a future title shot against whoever wins it, on Simpson's own terms. Neither the third and fourth qualifying bouts nor the 1 August 2004 pay-per-view itself (WE ALL FALL DOWN, announced for the HP Pavilion in San Jose by commissioner Oslo but referred to as 'San Diego' by Simpson in this same broadcast -- an unreconciled discrepancy in the source, reported as written) survive in this wing's own held record.

name: GCW, 23 July 1999

matches.note: Announced as a tag match (Stanley and Derek Walker vs. Karasopolis and a mystery partner) but wrestled as a singles bout after Stanley claims Walker is injured; an unnamed giant runs in for Karasopolis and the referee calls for the bell, awarding Stanley the match by disqualification. Tommy Kain, presumed sidelined by a car-crash injury, reveals it was faked and strikes Karasopolis with a crutch beforehand.

appearances.source: Refereed the match, distracted at ringside by both valets before calling for the bell.

notes: Ken Stanley wins by disqualification after an unidentified giant runs in on Viktor Karasopolis's behalf, closing on a cliffhanger over the giant's identity that this record's own surviving documents do not resolve. Tommy Kain, believed sidelined since a car crash, reveals the injury was faked and helps Stanley by striking Karasopolis with a crutch.
